data.name: Ashwathama
data.long_meaning: Ashwatthama, also known as Duryodhana's brother, was a great warrior and a key figure in the Mahabharata. He was born from the divine Ashwattha tree and hence the name 'Ashwathama'. He is revered for his valor and unwavering devotion to Duryodhana.

data.cultural_impact: Ashwatthama holds a significant place in Indian mythology and literature due to his predominant role in the Mahabharata, a Sanskrit epic that is among the oldest surviving texts of Hinduism. The story of his unwavering loyalty to Duryodhana, his brother, and involvement in the great battle of Kurukshetra is still revered in Indian culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Ashwatthama is believed to represent the indomitable spirit and the unshakable devotion to one's cause. He symbolizes the ultimately selfless and unwavering nature of a true warrior, who is ready to sacrifice everything for his beloved and worthy cause. This spiritual significance serves as an inspiration for many in Hinduism and beyond, who seek to embody the warrior spirit and unwavering devotion in their own lives.

historical_references.reference: Ashwathama is believed to be the son of Dhaumya, a sage, and Urvashi, a celestial nymph. He is a central figure in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. In the epic, Ashwathama is a great warrior and is a cousin and trusted friend of Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Kuru kingdom. However, in the great Kurukshetra war, Ashwathama is filled with jealousy and anger towards the Pandava brothers. After the war, he performs a ritual to obtain immortality, but a curse results in his immortality being incomplete, leading to his eternal suffering.

Ashwathama is also mentioned in the Puranas, a collection of Sanskrit texts. In one story, Ashwathama is the commander of the armies of King Yudhishthira during the war against the Asura king, Vrishadhvaja. Ashwathama's army is defeated and he is forced to flee. In his desperation, he performs a ritual to obtain the invincibility boon, but in doing so, he inadvertently disturbs the peace of the gods, leading to the great cosmic war known as the Devasura Samudra.

modern_usage.modern_context: In Hindu mythology, Ashwathama is a legendary warrior who is known for his bravery and loyalty. He is mentioned in the Mahabharata, one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India. Ashwathama's modern context is seen in various forms on different platforms. In television, he is portrayed in Indian mythological shows and serials, keeping the ancient tales alive for new generations. In literature, Ashwathama is the protagonist of several contemporary works, such as 'The Ashwathama Saga' by Dr. S.S. Rajamouli and 'Ashwathama's Curse' by S.R. Subramanya. In the gaming world, Ashwathama appears as a playable character in various games, such as 'Mahabharata: Rise of the Kauravas' and 'War of the Vishwamitras'. The modern usage of Ashwathama's name has seen a surge in popularity across these three platforms.

name_in_real_life.story: Lakshmi Ashwathama from Delhi, India embodies the meaning of Ashwathama - "Horse among men". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Ashwathama is a revered figure in Hindu mythology, known for his unwavering devotion to Duryodhana and his bravery on the battlefield of Kurukshetra. His name, derived from the horse Ashva, symbolizes the steadfastness and strength of a loyal warrior. Additionally, Ashwathama is believed to possess the power of immortality, represented by the tree Asvattha or the Pipal tree, symbolizing endless life and spiritual growth.
